data.title: List commands return one page of 100, with the real total and the offset beside it
data.why: An agent's tool output is cut at roughly 25k tokens and it is cut silently: what comes back parses, looks whole, and is missing most of the board, so the agent answers on a fraction while believing it saw everything. task list --json was 1303k tokens at 4000 tasks, fifty-two times the budget. A page plus tasksTotal and tasksOffset turns that into something actionable - the agent can see it holds 100 of 4000 and either narrow the filter or walk with --offset. 100 rather than 200 because this repository's own tasks run 1100 bytes each, where the ceiling is 93; 200 only fits the leanest board. At 4000 tasks task list --json is now 50 KB and board --summary 29 KB.
data.rejected: A cap per column on the board: ten columns of a hundred is a thousand tasks, which is the response the cap exists to bound.; Limit without offset: the agent could see it had a slice but had no way to ask for the rest, so its only move would be to narrow the filter and guess.; Capping the length of each record at write time: it refuses what a person wrote, and in an append-only journal a refusal is a lost thought. prime already caps at output, which is where the fix belongs.
